quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When you see an accident ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived yet.

questions.explanation: Only stop at an accident if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not go to accident scenes just to look.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.

questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on your mirrors because they do not show directly behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: When a school bus stops on the road to pick up or drop off children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its lights flashing and stop arm out, you must stop completely. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the arm is pulled back. Even after the bus starts moving, wait until you are sure no children are crossing in front of you.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Which one has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, you must yield to a vehicle coming from the right.

questions.question: It starts raining while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive close behind the car ahead of you.

questions.explanation: When heavy rain reduces what you can see, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull to the side of the road and stop until it improves.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to cars driving straight toward them. You can only turn left when you can do so safely without affecting oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass in which of these places?

options.text: In the middle of a curve.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, in curves, or in no passing zones. Only pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Only vehicles with special disability plates or placards may park in spaces marked for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: Parking spaces marked "Reserved for Persons with Disabilities" can only be used by vehicles with disability license plates or disabled parking placards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A downgrade or hill is coming.
The road ahead will become narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: A downgrade or hill is coming.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep or long downgrade is ahead. The hill may have sharp curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, no right turns are allowed.

questions.question: When can you pass on the right shoulder of the road?

options.text: When the car in front is driving too slowly.
When the car in front is turning.

questions.explanation: You cannot drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle. Never pass on the right shoulder.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and nerve or muscle issues. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that affects your driving ability.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens and/or flashing lights, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and sirens, you must immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let following cars pass.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous. If you're on a two-lane road and traffic backs up behind you, pull over to let other vehicles pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: When traffic moves at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Travel at the same speed as other traffic (within posted limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed cannot crash into each other. Accidents happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.

questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to be alert and able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Leave the car and go find help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car because rescuers are more likely to find you there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car because rescuers are more likely to find you there.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. Rescuers are more likely to find you if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm can be unsafe.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass, even if it is dangerous.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.
